title: StrictLocalInjectiveSourceRestriction
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$, $s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$, $K$, $n$, $J$ and $q$
be as in [def-weil-pbc-strict-local-injective-source-comparison], and let $Q$ be
strict-local neighbourhood geometry [def-weil-pbc-strict-local-neighbourhood-geometry].
Use the specific constructed $A_i$, not arbitrary source isomorphisms. For each $i$,
the canonical source leg $\ell_i$ [def-weil-pbc-canonical-derived-cohomology-germs]
followed by the global-sections homology map $m$ of the derived strict-local mate
[def-weil-pbc-strict-local-mate-projection-data] is
$\ell_i m=A_i r_{Q_i,t_i,p} c_p T^{-1}$, where $r$ is termwise sections restriction,
$c_p$ is representativeSectionsComparison
[lem-weil-pbc-injective-sections-pullback-comparison], $p$ is the limit projection
and $T$ is strictLocalBaseChangeTargetIso. This only asserts the cone-leg equation
for the canonical comparison; it asserts neither transition naturality nor
invertibility of $c_p$.

proof.text: Represent a source morphism by a Hom-complex cocycle into f_*J using K-injective localization. Applying homology, evaluating the free generator and taking the canonical germ gives the class of the same section. The unique strict-local stalk restriction is characterized by its neighbourhood germ legs. Q.first and Q.over identify both components with the fixed cone leg.

Compute the derived units and counits on J, expand the mate and cancel the intermediate unit and counit by the adjunction triangle identities. On sections this is sectionsPullbackNat along the cone leg followed by the inverse composition comparison. Take homology and retain the derived-sections unit at the limit: this is r followed by c_p. Exact inverse image commutes with homology; exact strict-local sections and Leray give T. Transport by q preserves this identity. No injectivity at the limit or continuity is used.
